title: At v6.2.2-dev.74 stages 1–7 of the auth scope have shipped: data model, decision model, positional deletion, enforcement, groups, conditions and the read path
content:
Status recorded from the spec's implementation plan at v6.2.2-dev.74 (the spec at v6.2.2-dev.47 still said only stage 1 had shipped):

| Stage | What | Flag |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Auth data model with backfill for legacy documents, the four actions and reducer, version-1 validation, persistence through save/load and versioned replay | — |
| 2 | Decision-model surface and the store's append condition | — |
| 3 | Document decision model replaces the document meta cache (positional deletion) | `documentDecisions` |
| 4 | Auth projection: admission, replay, re-evaluation | `authEnforcement` |
| 5 | Group principals: `powerhouse/reactor-group`, derived groups projection, group-reference relation, cross-document re-evaluation | `authGroups` |
| 6 | Condition evaluators with position-correct scope state | `authConditions` |
| 7 | The read path: reads routed through the registered decision model, policy-named groups served to the policy's audience | (each piece rides the flag it completes) |

Two stage-3 limits once listed as deliberate — `replayDocument` applying denied operations, and the read surface hiding a deleted document instead of serving the boundary state — turned out to have shipped with stage 4, and stage 7 verified them by exit test after clearing two remaining defects (revision one short after a trailing denied operation; a *denied* delete still marking snapshot rows deleted).

What remains is **stages 8–10**: the reactor client's reads are gated by the policy, but the host still has an authorization system of its own — private permission tables deciding sync serving and every read at the GraphQL boundary. Until those three stages land, `authEnforcement` cannot be turned on for a fleet that uses the tables, because every document's policy is uninitialized and an uninitialized policy allows everything. The Cookbook records the practical side: `group-principals` and `scoped-reads` need releases carrying the `authGroups` stage and the stage-7 read path, which at the time of writing meant running them through the monorepo's `test/recipes-e2e` link harness against a local checkout rather than the `dev` dist-tag.
